pathway.title: Magnera Corp — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Leverage is high, and whether it looks acceptable depends on the issuer's adjustments. Net debt of USD 1,621 million is 6.48x reported EBITDA of USD 250 million and 4.36x adjusted EBITDA of USD 372 million, so USD 122 million of add-backs, mostly restructuring and non-cash charges, decides the picture; creditors should lean on the reported figure until restructuring charges stop. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation X1; calculation X10

- Cash generation is the binding weakness. Free cash flow was USD 36 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 32 million in nine months of fiscal 2026, because cash interest, restructuring, taxes, capital spending and working capital absorb most of the EBITDA, so the issuer's outlook of USD 90 million to USD 110 million for the year needs USD 58 million to USD 78 million in the fourth quarter. Reported EBITDA covered cash interest only 1.70x in fiscal 2025, and 35.91% of principal is floating-rate, so a rate rise reaches that thin cover directly. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation X3; calculation X5; calculation X6; calculation X9; calculation X31

- The maturity profile is the main support. No debt matures until the 2029 notes of USD 500 million in October 2029, 74.57% of principal falls due in 2031, and cash of USD 280 million plus the USD 350 million revolver commitment gives USD 630 million on a commitment basis, so near-term liquidity is adequate while revolver availability itself is not stated. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation X7; calculation X8

- Business quality is average, not strong. Net sales of USD 3,204 million, over a thousand customers and consumer end markets give breadth, but adjusted EBITDA was only 11.05% of sales in fiscal 2025, selling prices follow raw material costs with a lag, and ten customers make up 42% of sales with many lacking long-term arrangements, so margin depends on pass-through timing rather than pricing power. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation X11; calculation X22

- Financial policy is mixed. There is no controlling sponsor, no dividend or repurchase in 2026 and USD 65 million of debt was repaid, which supports creditors; against that, internal controls over financial reporting were judged ineffective and management says it intends to pursue acquisitions, which could add debt. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation X20

- The primary downside path is a raw material pass-through squeeze, not a liquidity gap. A loss like the USD 14 million Americas price-cost shortfall of fiscal 2025 would cut adjusted EBITDA to USD 358 million, lift net leverage to 4.53x, cut cover of interest expense to 2.37x and take the free cash flow outlook to USD 76 million to USD 96 million, which slows deleveraging and tightens refinancing rather than exhausting cash. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 17; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ef20079553_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation X15; calculation X16

runs.text: Scale and breadth are the first strength. Net sales of USD 3,204 million across 45 plants and over a thousand customers, weighted to personal care and consumer products, spread volume risk across end markets and regions, which supports cash flow stability, although the price-cost lag limits the benefit. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation X22

The second strength is the debt calendar. The term loan and notes carry no financial maintenance covenants, nothing matures before October 2029, and USD 630 million of cash and revolver commitment sits against no near-term obligation, so an earnings dip does not trigger a covenant default and the issuer has time to repair leverage. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation X7; calculation X8

The third strength is evidence that savings are arriving. The synergy and cost reduction add-back fell by USD 25 million over three releases and the third quarter price-cost spread was USD 11 million favourable, which raises EBITDA without volume, and the issuer has repaid USD 65 million of debt and paid no distribution since the merger. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-02-05_ef20064605_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 6; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ef20079553_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation X19; calculation X20; calculation X23

The first weakness is leverage that relies on add-backs: net leverage of 6.48x reported and 4.36x adjusted, so an EBITDA miss of 5% would lift net leverage to 4.59x. The second is weak free cash flow, USD 32 million in nine months, which makes deleveraging depend on the fourth quarter and on working capital. The third is thin margin with a weak Rest of World segment, whose adjusted EBITDA margin was 8.70% against 13.82% in the Americas, so Europe's soft volumes pull group earnings down. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation X1; calculation X5; calculation X12; calculation X28

The fourth weakness is reporting quality: the auditor's adverse opinion on internal control and management's ineffective disclosure controls reduce reliance on every reported ratio. The fifth is the stated intent to pursue acquisitions while debt stands at USD 1,901 million, which could raise leverage before the current debt is reduced. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 20; Business & governance (CP-1A)

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The only transaction the documents describe is the merger completed on November 4, 2024, in which Treasure Holdco, then a wholly owned subsidiary of Berry Global Group, merged with Glatfelter, which was renamed Magnera; Treasure was the accounting acquirer and Berry's former shareholders received 90% of the combined company. At closing the company arranged a USD 785 million term loan, issued USD 800 million of 7.25% first priority senior secured notes and put in place a USD 350 million revolving credit facility, and Glatfelter's USD 500 million of 4.75% first priority senior secured notes stayed in place. The proceeds retired part of Glatfelter's debt and funded a USD 1,111 million cash distribution to Berry. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, pages 24–25

No new debt issue, acquisition or business disposal is stated after the merger. The company repaid USD 65 million of the term loan and the 2031 notes in the nine months to June 27, 2026 and sold one Rest of World facility in the quarter ended June 27, 2026, recording a USD 7 million loss and receiving USD 7 million of proceeds. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C9

fields.value: Financial foundation for Magnera Corp (magn), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the statements, debt, liquidity and leverage figures that later modules read, taken from the annual report for fiscal 2025 and the three quarterly reports and releases of fiscal 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Magnera Corp is heavily leveraged: net debt is 6.48x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA, or 4.36x the issuer's adjusted EBITDA, so creditors depend on those adjustments being repeatable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Nine-month free cash flow was USD 32 million after USD 44 million of capital spending, against USD 1,901 million of debt and USD 280 million of cash at June 27, 2026. No debt matures before 2029 and the USD 350 million revolver has no borrowings, but how much of it is available is not stated. The documents state no event after the balance sheet date that changes net debt.

fields.value: Leverage is high on every basis and is lower only if the issuer's adjustments are accepted. Total debt at carrying value is USD 1,901 million, 7.60x reported EBITDA of USD 250 million and 5.11x adjusted EBITDA of USD 372 million. The USD 122 million gap between the two measures is restructuring, non-cash and other charges the issuer excludes, and the issuer's pro forma figure of USD 405 million adds USD 35 million of synergies that are not yet in results. Reported EBITDA is therefore the primary basis here and adjusted EBITDA the best case.

fields.value: Cash generation is lumpy and weak against the debt load. Free cash flow on the cash flow statement was USD 36 million in fiscal 2025, not the USD 126 million the annual report shows, which adds USD 90 million of operating cash flow earned before the merger. Over nine months of fiscal 2026 it was USD 32 million, made up of USD 73 million in the second quarter, an outflow of USD 13 million in the first and an outflow of USD 28 million in the third. The outlook for the year of USD 90 million to USD 110 million of free cash flow therefore needs USD 58 million to USD 78 million in the fourth quarter. Working capital absorbed USD 34 million in nine months against USD 119 million a year earlier, which the quarterly report names as the main reason operating cash flow rose by USD 69 million.

fields.value: Liquidity looks adequate near term but cannot be verified from the filings. Cash of USD 280 million, of which about 58% is held outside the United States and is repatriable without significant restrictions according to the issuer, plus the USD 350 million revolver commitment gives USD 630 million on a commitment basis. Letters of credit and any borrowing base are not stated, so availability may be lower. Nothing matures until the 2029 notes of USD 500 million, followed by USD 1,466 million in 2031, so the refinancing exposure is nearly three years away.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Definitions and data quality need care. Three measures carry more than one figure: EBITDA (reported against adjusted), free cash flow (annual report against cash flow statement) and the debt repaid in the nine months (USD 63 million in the narrative against USD 65 million in the cash flow statement). Management also states that its disclosure controls were not effective at June 27, 2026, and that material weaknesses were reported at fiscal year end 2025, so the latest quarterly figures carry more reliance risk than a clean control record would. Receivables are also sold through customer supply chain financing programs whose size is not stated, which can move operating cash flow between periods without changing debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business, transaction, ownership and governance fact pack for Magnera Corp (magn), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is who owns and governs the company, what it sells and how it earns, the merger that created it, and how its financial policy and reporting bear on creditors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Magnera has no controlling sponsor, so creditors depend on management's own financial policy, which has been creditor-friendly since the merger: debt repaid, no shareholder distributions and a lower capital spending plan, set against material weaknesses in financial reporting controls.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is a large but thin-margin supplier of nonwoven materials to consumer end markets, with USD 3,204 million of net sales in fiscal 2025, ten customers making up 42% of sales and prices that follow raw material costs with a lag. Detail on the board, the shareholders and related-party terms sits in a proxy statement that was not supplied.

fields.value: - The owners are dispersed, so there is no sponsor whose willingness to support the debt can be assessed. At the merger in November 2024 Berry's former shareholders received 90% of the combined company and Glatfelter's shareholders kept 10%, and fewer than 62 holders of record are reported; no holder with a controlling stake is named in the documents read.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Financial policy since the merger is creditor-friendly on the evidence available. The company repaid USD 65 million of term loan and 2031 notes in the nine months to June 2026, its cash flow statements show no dividends or share repurchases, and its capital spending outlook for the year fell to USD 60 million from USD 80 million. The USD 1,111 million cash distribution to the former parent at the merger was paid out of new borrowings, so today's USD 1,901 million of debt reflects that transaction rather than later behaviour.

The figure fell from USD 60 million at the first quarter release to USD 48 million at the second and USD 35 million at the third, though the add-back is management's own measure and the savings it counts are not audited.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The Rest of World segment is the weaker earner and the volume risk: its adjusted EBITDA margin was 8.70% over nine months against 13.82% in the Americas, and its organic volume fell 3% on soft European demand. Customer concentration adds to volume risk, because the largest customer was 14% of fiscal 2025 sales and the top ten were 42%, and many customers have no long-term arrangement and can change suppliers quickly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Reporting quality is the main governance weakness. The auditor gave an adverse opinion on internal control over financial reporting at fiscal year end 2025, and management reports its disclosure controls as not effective at each 2026 quarter end, with remediation tied to moving off legacy U.S. systems inherited from Berry that remain under a transition services agreement. Creditors cannot yet rely on the controls to catch an error, and a restatement would be the event that matters; none is reported.

fields.value: - Acquisition appetite is stated but not yet used. Management says it intends to pursue additional acquisitions at attractive post-synergy multiples, which would add integration risk and could add debt, but the documents describe no pending transaction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a creditor-friendly reading is the stated intention to pursue further acquisitions while debt stands at USD 1,901 million, together with controls that make reported progress harder to verify. The view would turn adverse on a debt-funded acquisition, any shareholder distribution or share repurchase, or a restatement, and would firm on remediation of the control weaknesses and further debt repayment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The only transaction the documents describe is the merger completed on November 4, 2024, in which Treasure Holdco, then a wholly owned subsidiary of Berry Global Group, merged with Glatfelter, which was renamed Magnera; Treasure was the accounting acquirer and Berry's former shareholders received 90% of the combined company. At closing the company arranged a USD 785 million term loan, issued USD 800 million of 7.25% first priority senior secured notes and put in place a USD 350 million revolving credit facility, and Glatfelter's USD 500 million of 4.75% first priority senior secured notes stayed in place. The proceeds retired part of Glatfelter's debt and funded a USD 1,111 million cash distribution to Berry.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No new debt issue, acquisition or business disposal is stated after the merger. The company repaid USD 65 million of the term loan and the 2031 notes in the nine months to June 27, 2026 and sold one Rest of World facility in the quarter ended June 27, 2026, recording a USD 7 million loss and receiving USD 7 million of proceeds.

fields.value: Module status for governance work: ready with limitations, because ownership, board independence and legal capacity could not be read.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor and governance risk level: Medium. The level is driven by weak reporting controls and a stated appetite for acquisitions, because those could mislead or add debt, which implies lower confidence in reported ratios and a possible rise in leverage; countervailing evidence is the absence of any controlling holder, of shareholder distributions since the merger and of any reported restatement. Further analysis needs the proxy statement and the debt documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit assessment of Magnera Corp (magn), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the business and financial profile, the main supports and weaknesses, the primary downside path and the signals to monitor, built from the supplied filings and the earlier modules' findings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Magnera's fundamental credit is weak to average: scale and stable consumer end markets support the business, but net leverage of 6.48x reported EBITDA and thin, uneven free cash flow leave creditors reliant on cost savings and an orderly refinancing before 2029.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash interest cover was only 1.70x in fiscal 2025 and nine-month free cash flow was USD 32 million against USD 1,901 million of debt, but nothing matures until October 2029 and net leverage is 4.36x on the issuer's adjusted EBITDA. That gives time to reduce debt, though a repeat of last year's price-cost squeeze would lift net leverage to 4.53x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation X1; calculation X3; calculation X5; calculation X15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leverage is high, and whether it looks acceptable depends on the issuer's adjustments. Net debt of USD 1,621 million is 6.48x reported EBITDA of USD 250 million and 4.36x adjusted EBITDA of USD 372 million, so USD 122 million of add-backs, mostly restructuring and non-cash charges, decides the picture; creditors should lean on the reported figure until restructuring charges stop.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation X1; calculation X10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash generation is the binding weakness. Free cash flow was USD 36 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 32 million in nine months of fiscal 2026, because cash interest, restructuring, taxes, capital spending and working capital absorb most of the EBITDA, so the issuer's outlook of USD 90 million to USD 110 million for the year needs USD 58 million to USD 78 million in the fourth quarter. Reported EBITDA covered cash interest only 1.70x in fiscal 2025, and 35.91% of principal is floating-rate, so a rate rise reaches that thin cover directly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The maturity profile is the main support. No debt matures until the 2029 notes of USD 500 million in October 2029, 74.57% of principal falls due in 2031, and cash of USD 280 million plus the USD 350 million revolver commitment gives USD 630 million on a commitment basis, so near-term liquidity is adequate while revolver availability itself is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Business quality is average, not strong. Net sales of USD 3,204 million, over a thousand customers and consumer end markets give breadth, but adjusted EBITDA was only 11.05% of sales in fiscal 2025, selling prices follow raw material costs with a lag, and ten customers make up 42% of sales with many lacking long-term arrangements, so margin depends on pass-through timing rather than pricing power.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation X11; calculation X22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Financial policy is mixed. There is no controlling sponsor, no dividend or repurchase in 2026 and USD 65 million of debt was repaid, which supports creditors; against that, internal controls over financial reporting were judged ineffective and management says it intends to pursue acquisitions, which could add debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The primary downside path is a raw material pass-through squeeze, not a liquidity gap. A loss like the USD 14 million Americas price-cost shortfall of fiscal 2025 would cut adjusted EBITDA to USD 358 million, lift net leverage to 4.53x, cut cover of interest expense to 2.37x and take the free cash flow outlook to USD 76 million to USD 96 million, which slows deleveraging and tightens refinancing rather than exhausting cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a better view is momentum: last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 354 million at fiscal year end to USD 372 million, the synergy and cost reduction add-back fell from USD 60 million to USD 35 million as savings reached results, net leverage on adjusted EBITDA fell from 4.65x to 4.36x, and management reaffirmed its free cash flow outlook. If adjusted EBITDA reached the guidance range of USD 380 million to USD 410 million, net debt would be 4.27x to 3.95x, which would move the credit to average. Management itself expects the lower end of that range, and USD 372 million is USD 8 million short of it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve on free cash flow at or above USD 90 million for the year, continued repayment and remediation of the control weaknesses. It would weaken if adjusted EBITDA stays below the low end of guidance, if the price-cost spread turns negative again, or if an acquisition is funded with debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and breadth are the first strength. Net sales of USD 3,204 million across 45 plants and over a thousand customers, weighted to personal care and consumer products, spread volume risk across end markets and regions, which supports cash flow stability, although the price-cost lag limits the benefit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second strength is the debt calendar. The term loan and notes carry no financial maintenance covenants, nothing matures before October 2029, and USD 630 million of cash and revolver commitment sits against no near-term obligation, so an earnings dip does not trigger a covenant default and the issuer has time to repair leverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third strength is evidence that savings are arriving. The synergy and cost reduction add-back fell by USD 25 million over three releases and the third quarter price-cost spread was USD 11 million favourable, which raises EBITDA without volume, and the issuer has repaid USD 65 million of debt and paid no distribution since the merger.

fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-02-05_ef20064605_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 6; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ef20079553_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation X19; calculation X20; calculation X23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first weakness is leverage that relies on add-backs: net leverage of 6.48x reported and 4.36x adjusted, so an EBITDA miss of 5% would lift net leverage to 4.59x. The second is weak free cash flow, USD 32 million in nine months, which makes deleveraging depend on the fourth quarter and on working capital. The third is thin margin with a weak Rest of World segment, whose adjusted EBITDA margin was 8.70% against 13.82% in the Americas, so Europe's soft volumes pull group earnings down.

fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation X1; calculation X5; calculation X12; calculation X28

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth weakness is reporting quality: the auditor's adverse opinion on internal control and management's ineffective disclosure controls reduce reliance on every reported ratio. The fifth is the stated intent to pursue acquisitions while debt stands at USD 1,901 million, which could raise leverage before the current debt is reduced.

fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 20; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Magnera supplies specialty nonwoven and related materials for hygiene, wipes, healthcare, filtration and food and beverage uses from 45 plants, with Americas 55.34% and Rest of World 44.66% of nine-month net sales. The customer base is broad by count but concentrated at the top, with the largest customer at 14% and ten customers at 42% of fiscal 2025 sales, so revenue is predictable in aggregate because the products are consumed in everyday goods, yet exposed to a single account moving volume. The merger of November 2024 created the current group and left no controlling holder, so support must come from the business itself.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation X12; calculation X22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue moves with raw material cost more than with demand: selling prices fell by USD 117 million over nine months on pass-through of lower resin and pulp costs and mix, while organic volume was down 1% and Rest of World volume down 3%. Cost flexibility comes from Project CORE plant rationalisation and merger synergies, which the issuer credits for a third quarter price-cost gain of USD 11 million, while restructuring and other activities cost USD 61 million in cash payments in nine months, so margin improvement is real but is being paid for in cash that does not reach debt service.

fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 18; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ef20079553_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation X26; calculation X27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion is poor: free cash flow was 11.35% of adjusted EBITDA in nine months of fiscal 2026. Capital additions were only 1.80% of net sales and the outlook for the year was cut to USD 60 million from USD 80 million, so the first call on cash after capital spending is restructuring and interest, and the room to cut capex further may be limited by the need to maintain 45 plants.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation X17; calculation X18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competition is a real constraint: the annual report names six competitors, some with greater resources, and says many customers can shift suppliers quickly because they hold no long-term arrangement, so price pressure can arrive when raw material costs fall as well as rise. Buyer power is the strongest force because ten customers account for 42% of sales. Supplier power is high because resin and pulp prices are set outside the company and are passed on only with a lag. The documents say nothing on the threat of new entrants or substitutes, so those forces are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation X22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Foreign exchange and tariffs are the macro factors that matter: translation and transaction exposure to the euro, Brazilian real and Argentine peso moved net sales by USD 105 million in favour of the issuer over nine months, and tariffs are named as an outlook risk, so a stronger dollar would reduce reported earnings and the dollar cover of interest without changing the underlying business.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On the nine factors of the financial profile, scale and market position is a strength, competitive advantage is average because no moat beyond scale and customer relationships is evidenced, and business diversification is average given regional and end-market breadth but concentrated customers. Cost and capex flexibility is average, margin stability is weak because spread swings by USD 5 million to USD 14 million a quarter or year against EBITDA of USD 372 million, and free cash flow stability is weak. Ability to refinance is average, supported by the debt calendar and limited by leverage and thin cover, liquidity is average because availability is not stated, and financial policy and governance is average, with creditor-friendly behaviour offset by weak controls.

fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation X5; calculation X11; calculation X23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The trend is improving but slowly: net debt fell USD 26 million in nine months, leverage on adjusted EBITDA fell from 4.65x to 4.36x mostly through higher EBITDA, and the main missing datapoints are revolver availability, cash interest for 2026 and the debt documents.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the issuer's own outlook is for free cash flow of USD 90 million to USD 110 million this year and adjusted EBITDA at the lower end of USD 380 million to USD 410 million, which at current net debt would put net leverage at 4.27x to 3.95x; delivery supports a move toward average credit quality, while a miss leaves leverage near today's level with the 2029 maturities approaching. Tailwinds are the savings from the merger and Project CORE and lower capital spending; headwinds are raw material inflation that management calls a significant spike, soft European volume, higher cost of floating-rate debt and the cash cost of restructuring.

fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-02-05_ef20064605_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ef20079553_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation X13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the 2029 notes of USD 500 million and the revolver fall due in 2029 and USD 1,466 million falls due in 2031, so creditors need leverage to be lower before the first maturity; management says it intends to refinance debt before maturity but market access cannot be assessed from the documents supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The realistic downside starts with raw material inflation, which management already describes as a significant spike. Because contracts pass cost through with a lag, the first operating break is a negative price-cost spread; the issuer's own history shows what that costs, with the Americas segment losing USD 14 million of spread in fiscal 2025 and USD 5 million in the second quarter of fiscal 2026. Repeating the larger loss against last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA of USD 372 million gives USD 358 million, net leverage of 4.53x and cover of interest expense of 2.37x, and cuts the free cash flow outlook to USD 76 million to USD 96 million, so the year's low end of USD 90 million is missed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management levers are lower capital spending, which is already USD 60 million, a slower pace of restructuring and the USD 350 million revolver. Resilience looks sufficient to avoid a liquidity shortfall because cash of USD 280 million is large against a squeeze of this size and nothing matures until 2029, so the consequence is slower deleveraging and a tighter market when the 2029 debt must be refinanced; the observable triggers are a negative price-cost spread, free cash flow below the low end of the outlook and adjusted EBITDA below USD 380 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Magnera presents an average business profile supported by scale, consumer end markets and a long debt calendar, but credit quality is constrained by net leverage of 6.48x reported EBITDA, thin cash interest cover and weak free cash flow. Cash-flow durability appears weak because cash interest, restructuring, taxes, capital spending and working capital absorb most of EBITDA. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on adjusted EBITDA reaching the guidance range and free cash flow reaching USD 90 million for the year. The primary downside path is a raw material pass-through squeeze that cuts EBITDA and slows deleveraging before the 2029 maturities. Further analysis would require the credit agreement and indentures, revolver availability, 2026 cash interest and the fiscal 2026 annual report.
